heroHeadline: Magyar in Brussels for €10.4B EU Funds Deal; Prosecutor General Defies Resignation Demand
heroSubtitle: PM Péter Magyar traveled to Brussels on May 25 to sign a political agreement unlocking €10.4 billion in frozen RRF funds, with an August 31 deadline driving urgency. Moody's issued a positive Hungary outlook on May 24, projecting GDP growth of 1.8-2.6% for 2026. On May 19, Prosecutor General Gábor Bálint Nagy joined President Sulyok in refusing to resign, deepening the constitutional standoff over Orbán-era institutional officeholders. FM Anita Orbán held Hungary's first bilateral meeting with Ukrainian FM Sybiha at NATO's Helsingborg Foreign Ministers meeting (May 21-22), marking a landmark diplomatic reset. Magyar also made a 'lightning visit' to Vienna on May 21, pledging asbestos cleanup and a joint Austrian-Hungarian cabinet meeting — signaling Hungary's return as a constructive EU partner.
footerNote: Tracker covers Hungary's political transition from Orbán's 2010 return to power through the 2026 post-election transition. Data reflects publicly available reports from verified sources.
